mechanism_claim: Under a large Top1-vs-Top2 quality gap, the marginal PIT-observable alpha of slots 2 and 3 is negative-expectancy because (a) the false-negative pool is structurally weaker on the same features that predict Top1 success (up_day_ratio, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50; standardized deltas −0.6 to −1.2), and (b) ruin probability compounds with position count while Top1 conviction capital shrinks. An adaptive rule that still fills 2 or 3 slots during high-gap regimes violates a regime-conditional Kelly logic and is falsifiable.
evidence_for: Numeric contrast table shows false_negatives sit below selected_winners on every momentum/quality proxy: up_day_ratio_20 (0.500 vs 0.625), vol_ratio_5_20 (1.179 vs 1.424), mom_20 (0.058 vs 0.163), px_vs_ma50 (0.056 vs 0.127), ma10_slope_5 (0.012 vs 0.027) — so Top2/Top3 candidates in high-gap regimes are not just 'slightly worse' but measurably degraded across the same PIT features that identify Top1.

8 of 27 archaeology cases are false_positive_ruin on B0 itself; ruin exposure scales multiplicatively with slot count (3× ruin probability for 3 slots vs 1× for 1 slot under independent ruin), so a high-gap regime that still fans out to 3 slots triples tail-loss surface.

pullback_pct median delta is +8.6pp (false_negatives at −7.3% vs winners at −15.9%) — the false-negative pool includes stocks with shallow pullbacks that look 'safe' but lack the deep-base momentum signature, reinforcing that gap-driven skipping is empirically supported.

is_b0_pick=false cases still achieve w4_return_bucket = large_win (e.g., entity_de1c657364, entity_535a1beed7), but only n=2 qualify as 'big winner' (≥8% AND ≥5pp above B0 median) — the rare payoff does not compensate systematic quality decay.

Base_duration_weeks median delta is −8 weeks for false_negatives; longer bases are characteristic of established leaders, so filling slots with shorter-base candidates violates base-effect compounding.
evidence_against: The single false_positive_ruin|selected_winner case (entity_6618d3e80c) shows Top1 can both win and ruin in different windows — concentration on 1 slot does not eliminate ruin, only reduces its frequency.

11 selected_winner cases demonstrate that B0 selection itself is reliable in >40% of archaeology; a 'concentrate to 1' rule still accepts ruin risk and forgoes positive-skew outcomes from slot-2 hits.
Diversification counterargument: 1-slot portfolio has higher variance than 3-slot under non-zero Top2 win rate; if Top2 win rate is even modest, variance reduction may dominate expected-return loss.

Method note restricts false-negative labeling to ≥8% W4 AND ≥5pp above B0 selected median — under that bar, false-negative rate is small (n=2 of 27), suggesting the gap-skipping penalty is rare rather than pervasive.

The numeric_contrasts are false_negative vs selected_winner, not Top1 vs Top2 directly — we lack an explicit Top2 quality score, so the 'gap' is inferred from a downstream cohort rather than measured at the time of selection.
falsifiable_predictions: Regime-conditional test: stratify all live candidates by Top1-Top2 quality gap (e.g., top-decile vs bottom-decile) and compare equal-weight-3 vs concentrated-1 vs concentrated-2 Sharpe. Predicted outcome: concentrated-1 dominates concentrated-2 dominates equal-weight-3 in the high-gap decile; rank order inverts or flattens in the low-gap decile.

Ruin incidence test: count false_positive_ruin events per slot deployed in high-gap regimes. Predicted outcome: ruin-event rate per dollar of capital deployed is non-increasing in position count only when the gap is large; under small gaps, ruin-event rate per dollar decreases with more positions (diversification benefit dominates).

W4 return variance test: portfolio W4 return std-dev should fall monotonically with slot count in high-gap regimes (1 > 2 > 3 in std-dev) but expected W4 return should fall faster than std-dev for slot 3 vs slot 1, producing lower Sharpe for the 3-slot allocation.

Interaction test: regression of realized W4 return on (slot_count × gap_bucket) should produce a significant negative coefficient on slot_count restricted to the high-gap bucket. A non-significant or positive coefficient falsifies the gap-conditional concentration hypothesis.

PIT-feature falsifier: if pre-entry up_day_ratio_20 of slot-2 candidate exceeds 0.6 AND vol_ratio_5_20 exceeds 1.4, then the 'large gap' classification should be overridden and slot 2 included — otherwise the rule is over-fit to the Top1-only cohort and will miss the entity_535a1beed7 / entity_de1c657364 archetype.

Ruin clustering test: false_positive_ruin cases cluster on snapshot_anon (e.g., snap_71486ed83c, snap_b8420124eb, snap_d0d57b1e40 each contain multiple ruins); a regime-aware capacity rule that throttles to 1 slot on those snapshots should reduce ruin-cluster P&L impact by >50% versus a 3-slot allocation.
policy_implications: Capacity rule should be encoded as a regime filter: capacity = 1 when Top1−Top2 gap > threshold τ (high-gap), capacity = 2 or 3 when gap ≤ τ (low-gap). Threshold τ should be set so the upper-tail false-negative rate (≥8% W4 AND ≥5pp gap) is below a calibrated break-even probability.

Economic meaning under fixed 3-slot capital: '1 position' = full Top1 conviction, max idiosyncratic risk, minimum ruin-multiplier; '2 positions' = Top1 + quality-tier hedge, partial ruin-multiplier, intermediate Sharpe profile; '3 positions' = forced dilution including a Top3 that by gap definition is the weakest, producing the worst risk-adjusted profile in high-gap regimes.

Distinguish capacity from sizing: capacity 1 means 100% of capital in Top1; capacity 2 with equal-weight means 50/50; the rule must specify allocation as well as count, because filling 3 slots at 33% each is economically different from 60/30/10 weighted.

Refutation protocol: any adaptive rule that defaults to 3 slots in high-gap regimes should be rejected a priori; empirical defense requires showing 3-slot allocation has higher Sharpe than 1-slot in that regime, which the archaeology does not support.

Reject the rule if a single high-gap snapshot shows 3 simultaneous false_positive_ruins (the worst outcome class for fixed-3-slot capital) — the archaeological frequency of ruin-clustered snapshots (≥3 ruins per snap_anon) implies 3-slot deployment in those snapshots is the dominant tail-loss path.

Monitor false_negative_big_winner rate as the cost of concentration; if it exceeds a calibration ceiling (e.g., >5% of high-gap regimes produce a missed ≥8% Top2), the gap threshold τ should be tightened to widen the 2-slot allocation band.
